findings.title: The earlier combination's FRESH-3 comparison (75 against 64, p = 0.03) is not against that arm's whole budget: its control stops at 75% of the combination's own cost
findings.explanation: replicate.py compares the secondary arm 'combination@deploy:fresh3' with arms['fresh3']['controls']['any'], the union whose largest budget is C2 = (T + D)/300 computed from THIS run's T = 127,280,000 (6 student and 5 teacher runs). The earlier combination was not produced by this run. By the same registered formula its loop (results/expertB.json: 9 student runs, 7 teacher runs) has T = 9 x 338 x 10^4 + 7 x 214 x 10^5 = 180,220,000, the 533,195 per task that the README itself quotes two paragraphs later ('1.8 x 10^8 in all'). Its C2 on FRESH-3 would be (180,220,000 + 30,000,000)/300 = 700,733 candidates per task. Generation 0 was never run above 524,267 on FRESH-3, i.e. 74.8% of that. The README lists '75 against 64 (20 against 9, p = 0.03)' in the same list and against the same 64 that it describes as everything generation 0 solves 'at any budget up to the whole training and deployment budget'; for this arm that description does not hold. The comparison is fragile exactly at this point: the last rung (228,969 -> 524,267) added 7 tasks to the control's union, 2 of them tasks the combination lacks.

findings.title: expert_dependence.py compares only the last attempt's batch, so it reports the filter symbol c2_2 as needing the newer corpus when the older corpus proposes it too
findings.explanation: Lines 97-98 take only the last attempt's batch (`[len(students) - 1]`) from the counterfactual replay on the older corpus. On that corpus the greedy proposal order is different, so a symbol can show up in attempt 1 instead of attempt 2. Attempt 1's batch is then banned for attempt 2, so the symbol is missing from the batch the script compares and gets counted as 'only with the newer programs'. For cycle 2 of expertB this is what happens to `filter (lambda x. gt (mod x k) 0)` (c2_2). Its 3 supporting programs (far/odds, far2/remove-mod-k k=2 and k=3) are identical in the older corpus and contain no cycle-1 symbol. On the older corpus it is proposed in attempt 1 with the same score (7) and the same 3 tasks. Only `tail (tail (tail xs))` (c2_1) really depends on the new programs: 7 of its 10 supporting tasks are slice-k-n programs that teacher1 found with c1_2.
findings.repro: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=<work>:<tree>:<tree>/exploratory/shift_loop_20261110 python3 <work>/find-loop-code/dep.py exploratory/shift_loop_20261110/results/expertB.json. The script replays cycles 1-2 with expert_dependence's own absorb/proposals and checks that the replay matches the recorded proposals. It then lists the supporting tasks of each cycle-2 symbol (new or old program, and whether the rewritten program contains a c1 symbol) and prints every attempt's batch on the newer and on the older corpus.
findings.observed: Replay equals recorded: ['tail^3', 'filter (gt (mod x k) 0)', '((add -1) -1)']. Support of the filter symbol: far/odds old, far2/remove-mod-k k=2 old, k=3 old, no c1 symbol in any of them; 'all 3 support programs identical in both corpora: True'. Older corpus, attempt 1: [('(lambda x0: bool. (((if x0) 1) 0))', 10, 7), ('((mul 2) 5)', 7, 5), ('(lambda x0: int. (lambda x1: list[int]. ((filter (lambda x2: int. ((gt ...', 7, 3)]. Older corpus, attempt 2: [('((add -1) -1)', 5, 4), ...]. Support of tail^3: 3 old drop-k programs plus 7 new slice-k-n programs from teacher1 that rewrite to c1_2. The stored results/expertB_dependence.txt says '1 of 3 symbols are proposed from the older corpus too' and lists the filter symbol under 'only with the newer programs'.
findings.effect_on_results: README, Expert iteration, configuration B, third bullet: 'two of the three cycle-2 symbols, tail (tail (tail xs)) and filter (lambda x. gt (mod x k) 0), are proposed only because of the programs the cycle-1 symbols added' should say one of the three, tail (tail (tail xs)) only. The older corpus also proposes the filter symbol (attempt 1, same score and tasks) and the constant -2 (attempt 2). The 'one recursive link' remains, but it is the tail^3 symbol alone. The line in expertB_dependence.txt is wrong for the same reason.
findings.fix: In the counterfactual, compare the union of the symbols proposed across all attempts, or replay the older corpus's own accept/reject sequence, instead of taking the batch at index len(students)-1. Also report, for each symbol, whether its supporting programs differ between the two corpora; that is the direct test of 'proposed only because of programs the cycle-1 symbols added'.

lenses.coverage:
I read hybrid.py, loop.py, expert.py, expert_ablate.py, expert_dependence.py, frontier.py, state_run.py, dream.py and the scoring and propose parts of compress.py, plus the engine's search loop and stop rule (rsi5/engine/bottomup.py). My scripts are in <work>/find-loop-code (patience.py, roundtrip.py, dep.py). Nothing was run on FRESH-4.

Checks that did NOT break:

(1) PATIENCE wrapper. I ran hybrid.solve in-process with the wrapper and with the plain engine stop rule, on full-vocabulary searches. Settings: train+near at budget 1000 with SCf, and validation, far, far2, fresh2 and compose24 at 600 with SCfR. The wrapper never fired, and terms, routes, candidates and to_solution matched on every task.

(2) The 'all' ablation against the final student. expertB_ablate row 'all' against expertB run 12: all 173 solved keys match, and program, route and to_solution are identical on every one. spec_without and serialise build the same vocabulary: same order, same types, and the nullary c2_3 = -2 becomes a constant in both.

(3) Ablation arithmetic. Cycle 1 gains 15 and loses 1. The no-cycle-1 ablation loses 23 = those 15 + 8 later solves, and every one of the 8 has a c1-derived symbol in 'used'. 9 learning solutions combine a c1-derived symbol with a cycle-2 symbol, 7 of them among the 8. All reproduce from the files.

(4) The 'used' / learned_in mechanism. _ASKED['last'] is the solution expression at StopSearch. Fused and R routes take the union of their parts. One gap: learned constants (nullary symbols such as c2_3 = -2) are never counted in 'used'. In expertB only 3 fresh1 programs use -2, all with used=[], so no reported count changes.

(5) Accounting. expertB: 9 student runs and 7 teacher runs equal the 16 timeline records, and (9*338*1e4 + 7*214*1e5)/338 = 533,195. For loopA2 and loopB2, 8580 and 8500 executions times 1e4/338 give 253,846 and 251,479. The second-loop run cap counts the dream-bank runs, which matches the reported 'run N of 24'.

(6) Information flow. In expert.run, the corpus, family_of and the gate read learning partitions only, and the ban list is learning-only. In loop.run_loop, usage and the cut read learning plus dream programs only. Dream tasks are built from learning programs on seeded random inputs; task names reach the worker only as an entropy seed.

(7) compress. Rewrite then expand on all 246 distinct recorded expert programs: no semantic mismatch and no size growth. Every stated score equals the size removed from the corpus minus the body without its binders; the difference from my first recount was exactly the number of parameters.

(8) Expert configuration A numbers and frontier. Configuration A matches: 15 screened out, harvest 84 and 84, nothing accepted. The frontierB2 rows at 10^4 match the loop's gen0 and best states program by program.

Latent, no effect on any reported number: state_run.state_spec passes no constants, so a nullary learned symbol would be dropped, but no loop library has one. CONST_WITNESS is never cleared between specs; this is harmless because witnesses are deterministic.

I did not test the R-route budget split in detail, dream-bank growth in the second loop, or expertB_R / expertB_1e5.

verdicts.title: expert_dependence.py compares only the last attempt's batch, so it reports the filter symbol c2_2 as needing the newer corpus when the older corpus proposes it too

findings.title: 'Sound' only means correct inside the value range of the task's examples. Some programs called sound are wrong for what the routine name means, but the reported comparisons are not affected
findings.explanation: fresh_inputs (oracles.py lines 265-276) only draws values between the smallest and largest value in the task's examples, and lengths between the shortest and longest example input. When the examples never contain a value that the routine treats specially, the audit cannot see that a program ignores it. The clearest case is a 'positions' task (the indices of non-zero elements) whose examples contain no 0. There the program `(range (length x0))` is called sound, yet it is wrong on any list that contains a 0. Other programs pass only because of threshold or modulus tricks that hold inside 0..16, for example `if x>=10 ...` on (modulo-k 10)(identify-is-mod-k ...), or `mod x 20` on (pow-base-k 4)(is-evens). The README states this range limit (line 85: 'inside the task's own range of lengths and values'), so the definition is disclosed. The counts below show how much it matters.
findings.repro: cd <tree> && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=<work>:<tree>:<tree>/exploratory/shift_loop_20261110 python3 <work>/wide.py gen0R_569881.json frontierB2_gen0_181775.json ; <work>/wide3.py ; <work>/wideall.py ; <work>/widereg.py   (work = <work>/find-audit). Each script re-tests programs the audit calls sound against every validated reading, on 250-600 random lists of length up to 12 (30 in the 'long' set) with values 0..40 or -20..40, using a step budget of 100000.
findings.observed: Held-out B (wide.py): first it reproduces trained 44 sound, generation-0 union 38, 10 tasks only trained, 4 only generation 0. In the wider test 0/10 trained-only and 0/4 control-only programs fail, at 0..40, at -20..40 and on long lists. On the 34 tasks both arms solve, 9/34 trained and 8/34 control programs fail at 0..40 (several only on [] or on the value 0). FRESH-3 (wide3.py): reproduces 71 against 64, 18 against 11. At 0..40, 0/18 trained-only programs fail and 1/11 control-only programs fail: prepend-k 10 then identify-is-mod-k, on input [37,34,8,23] the reference gives [0,0,0,0,0] and the program [0,0,1,0,1]. All 630 distinct sound programs in the exploratory result files (wideall.py): 89 fail on non-empty lists with values 0..40, per partition train 11/78, near 29/200, validation 12/34, far 0/26, far2 2/51, fresh1 8/67, fresh2 17/125, compose24 10/49. Registered restored run at 10^6 (widereg.py), as wide/sound/verified: train 19/23/23, near 64/70/72, validation 7/8/8, far 8/8/8, far2 18/18/18, fresh1 9/9/10, fresh2 17/18/28, compose24 1/2/2. Most of the corpus failures are on caesar-cipher-k-modulo-n tasks. Those examples only contain values below n, so a program like `x0` with k≡0 mod n, or `1-x` for k=1 n=2, is correct on the task's real domain. Those are not real errors.
findings.effect_on_results: No reported comparison changes. The held-out-B result 44 against 38 (10 against 4) in 'The combination' and 'Registered replication' still holds in the wider sense: every discordant program on both sides is also correct on wider inputs. The FRESH-3 primary result 71 against 64 (18 against 11) slightly favours the trained arm in the wider sense (18 against 10). The absolute 'sound' counts are upper bounds for correctness outside the example range. On the one case that is genuinely about meaning rather than domain, the registered FRESH-2 cell at 10^6 is 17 instead of 18: replace-all-k-with-n 2->10 then positions, solved as range(length).
findings.fix: Make 'sound' mean 'agrees on the task's own input range' explicitly in the README and in RESULTS_P1.md. Optionally, for routines with a special value (positions and 0, has-k/count-k/identify-k and k, the modulus of the mod routines), add that value to the fresh-input range even when the examples lack it.

(1) Recount. audit_all.py registered 100000 and 1000000 give exactly the restored rows of the RESULTS_P1.md extended-audit table: 19/19 51/51 3/3 4/4 15/15 5/5 14/21 1/1 at 10^5, and 23/23 70/72 8/8 8/8 18/18 9/10 18/28 2/2 at 10^6.
(2) checks.py. check_references (338/338, 11 tasks with several readings), check_agreement (60 programs, 4 coincidental, identical verdicts) and check_known_programs all pass in this copy. audit_p1 covers fresh1, far2 and compose24 (6+14+10+2+18+10 = 60).
(3) Coverage (cov.py). Every reading of all 338 tasks gets exactly 200 fresh inputs, all inside the reference's domain, so the vacuous `want is None: continue` path never fires. Only four tasks have a single output value: far/empty; (identify-geq-k 3)(empty); (mult-k 10)(is-odds); near/is-mod-k k=1. In each, the other answer exists only for [], which is an example, so the test is complete there. The two integer tasks with two outputs are counts of 0/1 or 0/2 by construction. No task has a k-parameter outside its example value range (kout.py).
(4) Multiple readings (multi.py). All 11 tasks with several validated readings were checked. The readings agree on the fresh inputs, except index-head, where they differ only in domain, and (rotate-k -2)(identify-k 1) and (slice 2 2)(count-k 10). On those last two, every program found in the result files fails both readings. No program is called sound only through a non-obvious reading. Single readings checked against names and examples (positions, odds with floored mod matching the DSL's Python %, dup, rotate) fit their meaning.
(5) Counterexamples printed by --list. I checked 8 by hand against the task examples and value ranges: identify-k -2 with 0 in range, identify-geq-k 7 then modulo-k 4, replace-all 3->-2 then is-odds on [13], replace-index then count, uniq then count-k 2, identify-is-mod-k 7 then is-evens, the has-k fold, and is-mod-k k=2. Each is inside the domain and the reference is right.
(6) Type pitfalls. verifier.verify has no type check (`result.value != expected`), and the audit's type check is top-level only, so a list[int] program on a bool-identify task would be called sound (typ.py shows True). But a scan of all 775 exploratory programs and 523 FRESH-3 programs found 0 element-type mismatches (typscan.py). Exceptions swallowed in validated() cost no task, since all 338 keep a reading.
(7) Wide re-test. Covered in the finding: no reported comparison moves.

I did not touch FRESH-4, confirm.py, deepen*, or the judge material.

verdicts.title: 'Sound' only means correct inside the value range of the task's examples. Some programs called sound are wrong for what the routine name means, but the reported comparisons are not affected
verdicts.evidence: I checked the mechanism myself. oracles.py fresh_inputs (lines 260-276) draws lengths only between the shortest and longest example input, and values only between the smallest and largest example value. The concrete case holds. In rsi5/results_p1/restored_fresh2.json, record 72 is ((replace-all-k-with-n 2 10)(positions)), solved with program `(lambda x0: list[int]. (range (length x0)))`. Its 10 public and hidden examples have values from 1 to 15 and contain no 0. The positions reference (oracles.py line 134) is `[i for i,x in enumerate(xs) if x != 0]`, so the audit can never draw a 0 and calls the program sound, yet it is wrong on any list that contains 0. 88 of the 100 FRESH-2 tasks have a 0 in their examples, and the other positions tasks (add-k, append-k, identify-k then positions) all go down to 0. So this one task's examples lacking 0 looks like chance, not a domain restriction. The limitation is stated in both reports. README line 85: 'The fresh inputs stay inside the task's own range of lengths and values'. RESULTS_P1.md line 252: 'run on 200 fresh inputs inside the task's own input range'. I did not rerun the reviewer's wider-input recounts (89/630 and so on). By the reviewer's own account they move no comparison, and many of them are caesar-cipher domain artefacts rather than real errors.
verdicts.effect_on_results: Under the definition as written, no reported number is wrong. Under a stricter 'meaning' definition, the restored FRESH-2 cell at 10^6 in RESULTS_P1.md's extended-audit table would be 17/28 instead of 18/28, and the sentence 'should be read as 18, not 28' would read 17. No verdict, prediction or held-out comparison changes: 44 vs 38 (10 vs 4) and the FRESH-3 71 vs 64 (18 vs 11) stay as reported, as the reviewer also states.
verdicts.fix: Optionally add one sentence near README line 85 and RESULTS_P1.md line 252 saying that 'sound' gives no guarantee outside the example range. Name the replace-all-k-with-n 2->10 then positions case (range(length), whose examples contain no 0) as an instance where FRESH-2 at 10^6 would be 17 under a wider test.

findings.title: The 2,386-program corpus in RESULTS_P1.md is not pinned by the test that cites it
findings.explanation: In the 'Second review' table, RESULTS_P1.md cites test_closures_agree_on_the_programs_the_engine_builds for a corpus of '2,386 programs from the engine's own pools, both vocabularies'. The row before it says the earlier test's pinned count is now asserted (191). The new test does not assert 2,386. It asserts only len(programs) > 1000 for each vocabulary and agreed > 5000. A change to the engine that shrank the pools, or changed what they hold, would leave the test green while the documented corpus no longer exists. This is the same defect the correction was meant to fix in the first test: a count that is quoted but not asserted.
findings.repro: No run needed (a run would need budget=4000, above the 2000-candidate limit for this review). rsi5/tests/test_evaluator.py lines 94-96 and 111: `engine.search(..., budget=4000)`, `self.assertGreater(len(programs), 1000)`, `self.assertGreater(agreed, 5000)`. No assertEqual on 2386 or on any count per vocabulary.
findings.observed: The only bounds are >1000 programs per vocabulary and >5000 agreeing evaluations in total. The 2,386 quoted in RESULTS_P1.md appears nowhere in the test.
findings.effect_on_results: The sentence in RESULTS_P1.md's 'Second review' table, 'a second test admits no excuse on the corpus that matters: 2,386 programs', describes a corpus the test does not hold fixed. It should say the corpus is at least 1,001 programs per vocabulary, or the test should assert the count for each vocabulary.
findings.fix: Assert the exact program count for each vocabulary (the two counts summing to 2,386) and the exact agreed count, the same way the 191 is asserted.

lenses.coverage: Read in full: rsi5/guard.py, rsi5/phase1.py, rsi5/tests/test_guard.py, the worker modes of rsi5/tests/guard_attacks.py (early_workers, late_worker, dead_worker), the closure-agreement test in test_evaluator.py, and the 'Second review' section of RESULTS_P1.md. One finding: the 2,386 count is quoted but not asserted. Executor checks that did NOT break: (1) A worker that dies raises BrokenProcessPool in the driver, because concurrent.futures never replaces a worker and max_tasks_per_child is not set. An initializer that raises also breaks the pool. So 'a worker that dies fails the run' holds. (2) On Python 3.13 with the fork start method, the executor starts all its workers at once rather than forking them on demand. worker_pool's warm-up map also forks before the first partitions.load. I found no path to a late fork. I did not check whether Python 3.11 (the Actions version) forks lazily: that would mean reading the stdlib, outside the allowed tree. (3) Even a late worker would refuse every task: the check uses guard.preloaded() after seal_task_data(), which counts rsi2/rsi3 modules, and every partitions.load branch imports rsi2 or rsi3. test_worker_forked_after_the_tasks_refuses_to_search uses a plain multiprocessing.Pool, not worker_pool, so it tests only _init_worker and run_task. That is consistent with what it claims. (4) test_dead_worker_fails_the_run can fail: under the old multiprocessing.Pool layout, map would hang until the 900-second timeout. Over-blocking, as far as I checked by reading: guard._open_directories lists the absolute /proc/self/fd and does not recurse in the hook. A descriptor that is not a file (pipe, socket) has no path base and is not refused. I found no path the driver or a worker must open that the fail-closed rule refuses. I ran no mutation tests and no attack runs. I did not finish the first lens, an undeclared route through the guard: after the safety classifier stopped one of my responses, I chose not to try out bypass techniques against the hook. That lens is unreviewed, not cleared, and the absence of a finding there is not evidence that the guard has no undeclared route.

verdicts.title: The 2,386-program corpus in RESULTS_P1.md is not pinned by the test that cites it
verdicts.evidence: rsi5/tests/test_evaluator.py, test_closures_agree_on_the_programs_the_engine_builds: runs `engine.search(..., budget=4000)` for ORIGINAL and RESTORED, then asserts only `self.assertGreater(len(programs), 1000)` per vocabulary and `self.assertGreater(agreed, 5000)` per vocabulary. The test contains no 2386 and no exact count. The row before it does pin a count exactly: `self.assertEqual(eager_failures, 191)`. RESULTS_P1.md line 395 ('Second review' table) says: 'The count is asserted (191), and a second test admits no excuse on the corpus that matters: 2,386 programs from the engine's own pools, both vocabularies.' A grep of rsi5/ and the exploratory README finds 2,386 in that one sentence only, so no test, pinned note or disclosure holds it. I could not recount the corpus, because the test's budget of 4000 is above this review's 2000-candidate limit. The finding does not depend on the current count: the number is quoted in the document and nothing asserts it.
verdicts.effect_on_results: No experimental number or verdict moves. What changes is the meaning of one sentence in RESULTS_P1.md's 'Second review' table. '2,386 programs' describes a corpus the test does not hold fixed. The test guarantees only more than 1,000 programs and more than 5,000 agreeing evaluations per vocabulary. An engine change could shrink the pools, or change what they hold, and the test would stay green while the documented figure became stale. This is the same quoted-but-unasserted pattern the correction was meant to remove.
verdicts.fix: Either add assertEqual on the program count for each vocabulary (the two counts summing to 2,386), and on the agreed count, the same way the 191 is pinned, or reword RESULTS_P1.md line 395 to 'more than 1,000 programs per vocabulary (2,386 at the time of writing, not pinned)'.

findings.title: Under the harness's vocabulary cut (apoptosis A), several normal-form rules refuse terms whose replacement uses a symbol the cut removed, so the behaviour is not just dropped from the pools but cannot be reached at all
findings.file: rsi5/engine/normal_forms.py (rules for length/is_empty on nil and cons, sub/mod/div e e, mul e 0, eq/lt e e) as applied by exploratory/shift_loop_20261110/hybrid.py:_restrict and loop.py:cut
findings.explanation: NORMAL_FORMS.md says a refused term's replacement 'equals the refused form wherever the refused form is defined' and is built in no more symbols. That only holds if the replacement's symbols are in the vocabulary. The replacements `length nil -> 0`, `length (cons a b) -> add 1 (length b)`, `sub e e -> 0`, `mod e e -> 0`, `div e e -> 1` and `is_empty nil -> true` need the literal 0 or 1, or `add`. normal() checks the term's shape only and ignores the vocabulary. hybrid._restrict builds cut vocabularies from usage and keeps consumers like `length` while dropping `int:0` and `add`. The recorded best state of configuration B (results/loopB2_1e4.json best_keep['list'], README 'unused cut (best state, run 20 of 24)') keeps cons, nil, length, mul and int:1 but not int:0 or add. In that space, `length nil` is the only short way to write 0 and `length (cons k xs)` is the only short way to write len+1, and the filter refuses both. In the registered vocabularies (both have 0, 1, add and true/false) this does not happen.
findings.repro: cd tree && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=tree:tree/exploratory/shift_loop_20261110 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 <work>/find-normal-forms/demo_bestkeep.py (vocabulary = RESTORED restricted to loopB2 best_keep['list'], learned s12_* symbols left out; budget 2000; the filter switched to commutative order only for the comparison). Second demo: demo_cut.py (a cut without the literal 0).
findings.observed: length xs + 1, filter on -> length (map (λ. false) (cons -1 x0)), 1827 candidates (size 7). Commutative order only -> length (cons -1 x0), 139 candidates (size 4). prepend 0, filter on -> None after 2000 candidates (size 6 completed). Commutative order only -> cons (length nil) x0, 147 candidates. demo_cut.py: prepend-0, filter on -> cons (mod 1 (sub 1 2)) x0 at 365 candidates; filter off -> cons (length nil) x0 at 47.
findings.effect_on_results: Programs are lost only. There is no wrong solve, because every match is re-checked by the reference interpreter. Under a cut, the filter removes more than the cut itself does. So the README rows for cut states (Configuration B 'apoptosis' and 'unused cut (best state, run 20 of 24)' 122/127, 30/38; Configuration A 'apoptosis' and 'four more accepted steps' rows; F2 'symbols with the full vocabulary do as well as the best state with its cut'; the sentence 'The cut helps at 10^4 and costs at every larger budget') measure the cut combined with this filter interaction, not the cut alone. Those numbers may understate what the cut states can solve. The exact size cannot be measured within this review's budget limit. The README and NORMAL_FORMS.md should add 'the replacement is in the vocabulary' as a condition of the argument, or the cut should keep 0, 1, add and nil whenever their consumers are kept.
findings.fix: Make normal() aware of the vocabulary: refuse a left-hand side only when its replacement's symbols are available (0 or 1 literal, add, true/false, nil). Otherwise state in NORMAL_FORMS.md and the hybrid README that a cut vocabulary also loses these normal-form classes.

findings.title: Abduced constants (C) make `neg k` and `abs k` refuse literals whose negation or absolute value is not in the vocabulary; the `abs k` half is not disclosed
findings.file: rsi5/engine/normal_forms.py lines for neg/abs (`_lit(args[0])`), with exploratory/shift_loop_20261110/hybrid.py:_with_constants / init (abduced constants appended to integer_constants)
findings.explanation: The hybrid harness admits abduced constants (differences, ratios, output values in [-CONST_RANGE, CONST_RANGE]) as size-1 integer_constants. The engine treats them as `const`, so `_lit` is true for them. The `neg` rule then refuses `neg k` for every admitted k. The `abs` rule refuses `abs k`, where NORMAL_FORMS.md gives 'literal' as the replacement. When -7 is admitted and 7 is not, both size-2 ways to make 7 are refused. RESULTS_P1.md discloses only the `neg k` case and only for the registered literals 2..5. `abs k` is never a problem in the registered vocabularies, where abs(-1)=1 exists.
findings.repro: Same command, with script <work>/find-normal-forms/demo_cut.py (second part: vocabulary cons, nil, abs, neg, head with constants 0, 1, -3; task prepend 3; budget 2000).
findings.observed: constant -3 prepend-3 nf=True: None, size 8 completed. nf=False: cons (abs -3) x0 at 40 candidates.
findings.effect_on_results: Programs are lost only; there is no wrong solve. The abduced constant is usually the value the task wants, so the effect on reported counts is probably small and was not measured. The `neg k` part extends a defect already disclosed. The `abs k` part is new.
findings.fix: Refuse `neg k` and `abs k` only when -k or |k| is itself a constant of the vocabulary in use.

lenses.coverage:
I read rsi5/engine/NORMAL_FORMS.md, normal_forms.py, bottomup.py (how normal() is applied in _construct before counting, the vectorised and lazy-if paths, the de Bruijn order of fold and fix1 bodies, uses and lambda_of shifts, angelic rec), closures.py and the reference evaluator. I checked each rule by hand against the reference semantics: lazy if, left-to-right and/or, cons forcing both arguments, fold applying acc first, fix1 handing rec, budget and list caps. Each replacement is a subterm, a literal or a smaller term, and is at least as defined and no more step-costly. The fold rule (`body.head == 1` is acc) and the fix1 rule (index 1 is rec) match the engine's environment order (v, acc) and (v, rec). Rule chains such as if-not with repeated conditions, and length (cons) with add-0, terminate in kept terms.

Exhaustive dominance check with the engine itself (budget 2000, script <work>/find-normal-forms/dominate.py): every top-context behaviour built with the filter off, or with only the commutative ordering on, must equal, wherever it is defined, some behaviour of the same type and no larger size built with the filter on. I ran 7 restricted vocabularies covering arithmetic, list, boolean, map/filter/fold, unfold/index/zip/pair, fix1 and pair primitives, up to completed sizes 5 to 9. The only undominated behaviours were `neg 2` and `neg 1` when -1 is missing (the disclosed neg-k defect) and all-error terms. Once -1 was added, 0 were undominated in every vocabulary. Nothing in the registered vocabularies broke the argument beyond defects already disclosed: and/or order and strictness, neg k, and fix1 as a let-binding. I did not exercise fix1 bodies large enough to show let-binding sharing, and I did not measure how many registered or exploratory solves the cut interaction costs. The doc's remaining claims hold in the code: no β-redex, η-long form, fix1 only in the top context, refused terms not counted. I did not touch FRESH-4, confirm.py or deepen*.

verdicts.title: Under the vocabulary cut, normal-form rules refuse terms whose replacement uses a symbol the cut removed (length nil, length (cons a b), etc.)
verdicts.evidence: rsi5/engine/normal_forms.py refuses `length`/`is_empty` on any cons/nil argument, and `sub/mod/div e e`, `mul e 0`, `eq/lt e e`, by shape alone. It never looks at the vocabulary. results/loopB2_1e4.json best_keep['list'] has cons, nil, length, mul and int:-1,1..5, but not int:0 and not add (hybrid._restrict drops int:0 because it is absent from keep). My script <work>/verify-normal-forms/t1.py uses RESTORED restricted to that keep set, with no s12_* symbols, probe inputs from probes.inputs_for, and a budget of 2000. In a second run I relaxed only the length/is_empty rules. Filter as registered: len+1 is found as `length (map (λ. false) (cons -1 x0))` at 1922 candidates; prepend-0 gives None, completed size 6. Length/is_empty rules relaxed: `length (cons -1 x0)` at 102 and `cons (length nil) x0` at 106. The mechanism is real. Nothing in exploratory/shift_loop_20261110/README.md, NORMAL_FORMS.md or RESULTS_P1.md discloses it: NORMAL_FORMS.md says a rule 'can drop a behaviour class from the pools but not a program that solves a task', which holds only when the replacement's symbols are in the vocabulary.
verdicts.effect_on_results: No reported number is shown to move. The cut-state rows (B 'unused cut (best state, run 20 of 24)' 122/127 and 30/38; the apoptosis rows; F2 '38 against 32'; 'The cut helps at 10^4 and costs at every larger budget') are correct measurements of the system as built. The cut had already removed int:0 and add from the list space, and the filter only blocks the size-2/size-3 workarounds, so any solves lost are expected to be few and could be zero. The size of the loss is unmeasured. What changes is a sentence: the NORMAL_FORMS.md guarantee does not hold under hybrid cut vocabularies, and part of what the README calls a cost of the cut is this interaction.
verdicts.fix: Add a caveat to NORMAL_FORMS.md (the replacement must be in the vocabulary) and to the hybrid README's cut discussion: a cut vocabulary also loses the normal-form workarounds (`length nil` for 0, `length (cons k xs)` for len+1). Alternatively, the cut can keep int:0, int:1 and add whenever length, sub, mod or div are kept.

verdicts.title: Abduced constants make `abs k` (and `neg k`) refuse literals whose |k| or -k is not in the vocabulary
verdicts.evidence: In normal_forms.py, the `abs` rule refuses `_lit(args[0])` and so does the `neg` rule. Abduced constants are appended to integer_constants (hybrid._install / _with_constants), so the engine builds them as const literals. Script <work>/verify-normal-forms/t2.py uses the vocabulary cons, nil, abs, neg, head with constants 0, 1, -3, task prepend-3, budget 2000. Filter on: None, completed size 10. abs/neg literal rules relaxed: `cons (abs -3) x0` at 31. The `neg k` part is disclosed: RESULTS_P1.md says '`neg k` | Refused for every literal, though −2 ... are not literals', and NORMAL_FORMS.md says 'the literal -k where the vocabulary has one'. For `abs k`, NORMAL_FORMS.md gives only 'literal' as the replacement, and nothing covers abduced constants.
verdicts.effect_on_results: No reported count is shown to move. In the full RESTORED vocabulary, an abduced -k whose positive counterpart is missing (k > 5) can still be reached through add/sub/mul, costing one or more extra symbols. Only cut vocabularies without arithmetic lose it outright. The likely effect is zero to a handful of extra candidates per affected task. Unmeasured.
verdicts.fix: Disclose the `abs k` case next to the `neg k` row in RESULTS_P1.md / NORMAL_FORMS.md, extended to abduced constants. Alternatively, refuse `neg k` / `abs k` only when -k or |k| is itself a constant of the vocabulary in use.
